summary: The paper studies Mamba's in-context learning on random Markov chains, showing empirically that a single-layer Mamba learns the Bayes/minimax-optimal Laplacian (add-β) smoothing estimator, and provides a constructive theorem (Theorem 1) that a simplified 'MambaZero' can exactly represent this estimator for first-order chains, together with a lower bound (Theorem 2) showing hidden-dim·precision must scale as 2^k. The framing (Markov-ICL for Mamba) is a natural and useful extension of prior transformer-focused work, and the constructive proof aligning with empirically-observed learned parameters is the paper's strongest contribution. The main limitations are the narrowness of the formal result (first-order Markov, single-layer, L1 normalization instead of softmax), thin natural-language evidence, and a lower bound that (as written) does not clearly disentangle depth vs. dimension in a way that supports the strongest Mamba-vs-Transformer statement.
strengths: Clean theoretical contribution: an explicit constructive representation of Laplacian smoothing by a first-order MambaZero, whose construction (a_t≈1, w=k+1, count-orthogonality of b(ij)·c_t) is validated by matching empirically learned parameters (Figs. 4, 5) — this alignment is genuinely informative rather than a post-hoc curve fit.

Non-trivial architectural insight: the ablation showing that convolution is the load-bearing component in the Markov setting (Fig. 3a, MambaZero matches full Mamba while conv-free Mamba fails) is a crisp, mechanistically interpretable finding.
The Ω(2^k) hidden-dimension lower bound (Thm. 2) is a useful complement to Thm. 1 and provides a clean architectural comparison point against known transformer results (linear in k with depth 3).

Nice extension beyond pure Markovianity: the switching-Markov experiment (Sec. 5.1) demonstrates that a_t is used exactly as the theory suggests when the optimal predictor requires resetting counts — a strong sanity check of the mechanism.
Claims are generally well-scoped: the paper repeatedly notes that higher-order results are empirical, that comparisons are contextual rather than central, and that learning dynamics are out of scope.

key_concerns.issue: Theorem 1 is proved for MambaZero (a simplified architecture with L1-normalized prediction, no ReLU, no gating), not for the actual Mamba/Mamba-2 architecture used in Section 3's experiments. The paper's headline framing ('even a single-layer Mamba learns the optimal Laplacian estimator') therefore rests partly on an empirical extrapolation from a simplified model to the full model, and the gap is not sharply quantified. A reader could reasonably worry that softmax vs. L1 normalization and gating/ReLU change the achievable optimum non-trivially.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either (a) prove or approximately-prove the representation result for the full Mamba/Mamba-2 block (perhaps up to ε in KL), or (b) add an explicit head-to-head comparison of MambaZero vs. full Mamba at convergence on the exact Laplacian target (KL, not just training-loss curves) across state sizes S and orders k, so the reader can see how tight the simplified-model claim is as a stand-in for the full model.

key_concerns.issue: Higher-order representation is only supported empirically (Fig. 1b, Fig. 10a). The paper's contribution list emphasizes 'all Markov orders,' but the formal construction is first-order only, and the lower bound (Thm. 2) actually cuts against a dimension-efficient higher-order construction (needs d·p ≳ 2^k). This tension is acknowledged only briefly and deserves either a construction for order k or a more explicit statement that the upper bound is first-order.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a construction (even a lossy one, or one with d = O(S^k)) for kth-order chains, or tighten the statement of contribution 2 to 'first-order' and separate the empirical higher-order evidence from the theoretical claim in the introduction and abstract-equivalent framing.

key_concerns.issue: The Mamba-vs-Transformer conclusion drawn from Fig. 1 ('1-layer Mamba tracks the optimal estimator more sharply than a transformer') is used to motivate the paper but rests on a small, potentially under-tuned comparison. Transformer baselines are described generically; there is no explicit statement that both were tuned with matched compute, matched positional encodings, matched width, or with linear-attention/rotary variants that are known to help on synthetic count-based tasks. Given the induction-head literature the paper cites, a fair 2-layer transformer often does match on this task, so the sharpness of the qualitative claim needs firmer support.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report parameter-matched Mamba vs. 1L/2L/3L transformer sweeps with tuning budget, seeds and error bars for L1-to-optimal, across orders k∈{1..4}, and include at least one strong transformer variant (rotary + short conv, or a state-of-the-art hybrid). Alternatively, soften the comparative claim and clearly frame it as motivating context rather than a headline finding.

key_concerns.issue: Theorem 2's framing as 'recurrent models of any depth' is subtle: the theorem constrains the final-state size d and precision p, but multi-layer recurrent stacks can carry additional information across layers within a step, and the reduction from a depth-L recurrent model to a single H_t is not spelled out. The reader is left to infer whether the bound really applies to stacked Mamba layers.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add one paragraph in App. D formalizing how a depth-L recurrent model is folded into the (h_t, g_t) form so that d becomes the total per-step state footprint. State clearly whether the bound is per-layer state or aggregate state.

key_concerns.issue: The natural-language section (Sec. 5.2, Table 1) is thin: single dataset (WikiText-103), single model size (~14.5M params), single seed reported. The 11% vs. 2% perplexity gap is used to argue generality of the convolution finding, but this is a fragile empirical claim at this scale.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add seeds/variance for Table 1, at least one additional corpus (e.g., a subset of C4 or The Pile), and one larger model size, or explicitly downgrade the wording to 'preliminary evidence' in Sec. 5.2 and the conclusion.

key_concerns.issue: The 'Laplacian smoothing implies ICL' argument (end of Sec. 2.4) is somewhat rhetorical: matching the add-β estimator on a Dirichlet-prior random Markov process is what Bayes-optimal any-predictor does, so 'ICL' here just means the model does not memorize a single kernel. This is fine, but the paper occasionally slips into calling this an ICL 'ability' as if it were the richer few-shot ICL sense of Brown et al. — a distinction worth making explicit.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a short paragraph distinguishing Bayes-optimal in-context estimation on random Markov data from prompt/few-shot ICL, and be consistent in later sections about which sense is meant.

questions_for_authors: How tight is the MambaZero-to-full-Mamba gap? Specifically, when training the full Mamba-2 with softmax and gating on random first-order chains, does the achieved KL to the Laplacian target reach 0, or does it plateau at some strictly positive value that MambaZero avoids?

For higher-order chains (k>1), do you observe that the empirical d needed by trained Mamba grows in line with the 2^k lower bound of Thm. 2? A d-vs-k sweep at fixed precision would make this a much stronger claim.

In Thm. 2, does d refer to the per-step state width of a single Mamba block, or to the total per-step state summed across layers? If a depth-L Mamba can share the 2^k budget across layers, does the lower bound still bite for typical Mamba stacks?

The claim that convolution's importance diminishes with depth (Sec. 5.2) is intriguing but relies on 'other Mamba layers approximating convolution.' Do you have a direct probe (e.g., a per-layer ablation in a deeper Mamba) showing which layers take over the role convolution plays in the shallow model?

Transformer comparison: were the transformer baselines in Fig. 1 tuned with the same compute budget and comparable width/depth to Mamba? Would a 2-layer transformer with a short causal conv (Hyena/H3-style) match Mamba on Fig. 1b?
calibration_check: Claims are for the most part appropriately scoped — first-order construction is stated as such, higher-order and language claims are explicitly framed as empirical — but the introductory framing ('for all Markov orders') and the Mamba-vs-Transformer qualitative comparison run slightly ahead of the evidence and should be tightened.

significance.justification: Explaining an SSM mechanism via a known optimal statistical estimator is a genuinely useful contribution to the mechanistic-understanding line of work on Mamba; impact is real but bounded by the narrow (Markov, first-order) formal setting.

novelty.justification: First application of the Markov-ICL framework to Mamba, with a new constructive proof and a new 2^k dimension lower bound; the constructive alignment with learned parameters is a genuinely fresh angle rather than an incremental extension.

rigor.justification: The first-order construction and lower bound appear sound and the empirical verifications (a_t≈1, b(ij)c_t orthogonality) are the right diagnostics; however, the gap between MambaZero and full Mamba, and the depth-vs-state-size subtlety in Thm. 2, are not fully closed.

statistical_soundness.justification: Error bars over 5 seeds are shown for the main ICL curves, which is adequate for a synthetic setting, but the transformer comparison and the WikiText table are reported without variance and with limited tuning detail, weakening the strongest comparative claims.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper is generally careful: it flags that higher-order results are empirical, that learning dynamics are out of scope, and that comparisons are contextual — with only mild overreach in the intro's 'all Markov orders' framing.

clarity.justification: The problem setup, MambaZero simplification, and proof sketch are readable and well organized; some equation blocks (particularly the Mamba update in Sec. 2.2) are notation-heavy and would benefit from a compact schematic in-text.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure with problem setup, mechanism, theory, extensions, and conclusion; length appears appropriate for ICLR, and a Limitations section is present.

reproducibility.justification: Data-generation process, architectural equations, optimizer, and key hyperparameters (w, N, d, e) are specified, and appendices are referenced for details; anonymized links are the only obvious gap and are not counted against the paper.

related_work.justification: Positions the work well relative to the Markov-ICL transformer literature and to prior Mamba/SSM analyses; a slightly deeper treatment of Hyena/H3/conv-augmented attention lines would strengthen the 'convolution matters' story.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative figures — L1-to-optimal across orders, ablation on convolution, window-vs-order scaling, and the switching-Markov a_t behavior — each tied to a specific claim rather than decorative.

breadth_generality.justification: Formal results are first-order and single-layer MambaZero; higher-order, deeper-model, and language experiments are supportive but not decisive, so the 'general' framing outruns the evidence somewhat.

overall_recommendation.justification: A solid, mechanistically-interpretable theoretical contribution with matching empirics; a clear-accept-if-borderline paper at ICLR whose acceptance case would strengthen materially with a tighter full-Mamba result and a fairer transformer comparison.
